title: HEAT TREATMENT OF HYPO-EUTECTOID NITI ALLOY MANUFACTURED BY CGDS POWDER MIX DEPOSITION

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: deposit was cut using low speed saw to samples 5x6x7 mm and substrate was removed

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Deposit was 8/92 at.% Ni/Ti, with nickel having a much lower DE than titanium. fracture surface shows nicely that titanium, although severely deformed by the deposition process, still possess some plasticity and produces mixed ductile fracture with large areas of decohesion, whereas the nickel particles do not break at all and the fracture surfaces contain delaminated nickel particles where the nickel particles and the titanium matrix have separated. no connection between the nickel and titanium particles.

Experiments.Notes: As-spray. Titanium too brittle for hardness measurements. Nickel particles had a hardness of 281 HV0.01 in the deposit. (hardness values given seperately for Ni and Ti)

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Annealed in a tube furnace under flowing Argon protective atmosphere (1.2 l/min, purity 4N8) heated relatively slow to the desired temperature, held at 600°C for 2h. Left in the furnace to slowly cool in the Ar atmosphere.
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: deposit was cut using low speed saw to samples 5x6x7 mm and substrate was removed before annealing. The annealed samples were fractured and one piece of the material was used to prepare a metallographic sample by standard grinding and polishing techniques. No etching was used, but colloid silica (OPS from Struers) was used for the last polishing step, which provided also visible microstructure.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Deposit was 8/92 at.% Ni/Ti, with nickel having a much lower DE than titanium.  changes in the micro hardness in individual nickel particles and also in limited extend in titanium particles, which later show increase in hardness. A very limited amount of intermetallic phases was generated on the Ni-Ti interphase at both lower annealing temperatures. Point analysis showed that NiTi2, NiTi a Ni3Ti were firmed in minute areas

Experiments.Notes: Annealed at 600. Ti particle hardness was 307 HV 0.01, Ni particle hardness was 238 HV 0.01

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Deposit was 8/92 at.% Ni/Ti, with nickel having a much lower DE than titanium. An exception to the trend of decrease in hardness as annealing temperature increased due to diffusion of nickel atoms into the titanium, creating solid solution strengthened by substitution mechanism. new phases were formed rapidly around the nickel particles by mutual diffusion. By local chemical analysis compositions both Ti2Ni a TiNi3 were measured, likely resulting from NiTi decomposition. eutectoid mixture can be found occasionally, which indicates the presence of beta titanium solid solution. The diffusion speed is increased at elevated temperatures and with the possibility of beta titanium solid solution. After crossing the alpha to beta transformation temperature of titanium, the evolution of intermetallic phases was further increased.

Experiments.Notes: Annealed at 800. Ti particle hardness was 334 HV 0.01, Ni particle hardness was 141 HV 0.01

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Deposit was 8/92 at.% Ni/Ti, with nickel having a much lower DE than titanium. While solubility of nickel in alpha titanium is very low , in beta titanium it is above 10 %, which greatly promotes diffusion and new phases formation. titanium particles get enriched by nickel and gradually form network of eutectoid microstructure of α-Ti a Ti2Ni. The nickel particles are surrounded by rings of intermetallic phases and porosity. Parts of the nickel particles can be still seen unreacted. The matrix of this material consists of alpha titanium and eutectoid mixture. Eutectoid delamination between individual phases is possible in the areas of decomposed solid beta solution.  the shape of the porosity is changed to be more round and the individual titanium particles are well joined together

Experiments.Notes: Annealed at 900. Ti particle hardness was 367 HV 0.01, Ni particle hardness was 120 HV 0.01

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Deposit was 8/92 at.% Ni/Ti, with nickel having a much lower DE than titanium. nickel is fully dissolved in beta titanium matrix. The microstructure at room temperature is formed by titanium the eutectoid mixture and intermetallic phase Ti2Ni. The sample exhibits uniform and homogeneous character. The pores are nearly round which correspond with high diffusion rates.

Experiments.Notes: Annealed at 1000. Ti particle hardness was 326 HV 0.01, Ni particle hardness not reported (it was fully dissolved)
